column2: Tent, its vessels, altar and its vessels are all sanctified. Repeated anointing and sanctifying remain rather than being collapsed.
The selected text explicitly counts twelve rulers and connects them with the census. Both repeated these identifications remain.
Six wagons and twelve oxen correspond to one wagon per pair of rulers and one calf each. Covered is retained provisionally for the wagon descriptor.
column3: The precise construction denoted by the wagon adjective requires lexical review.

column2: The Lord's speech introduces the distribution of the gifts.
Moses receives the gifts for tent service and distributes to Levites according to each ministry, not in equal shares.
Moses receives wagons and oxen and gives both to the Levites.
Gershon receives two wagons and four oxen, according to service.
Merari receives four wagons and eight oxen through Ithamar. Aaron's priestly designation remains attached to the father's name.
Kohath receives none because sanctuary objects are carried on shoulders. The negative and its explanation remain.
Dedication gifts are presented on the anointing day and before the altar. Both presentations in the Greek are retained.
One ruler each day is repeated in the selected text. The draft preserves the repetition despite the compact shift to plural their gifts.
Day one names Nahshon, Amminadab and Judah in the selected sequence. The names agree with the provisional census register.
Nahshon's silver dish is 130 and bowl 70 sanctuary shekels; both contain oil-prepared flour. The dish's unit is clarified from the parallel bowl and verse 85.
Nahshon's one incense vessel is ten gold units and full of incense. No explicit gold shekel unit is imported.
Nahshon's whole burnt animals are one calf, one ram and one year-old male lamb. Calf represents the bovine animal without adding a second animal.
Nahshon's sin offering is one male goat. The from-the-goats wording remains.
Nahshon's deliverance offering has two heifers and five each of rams, male goats and year-old ewe lambs. The closing father-name attribution remains.
Day two names Nethanel son of Zuar for Issachar. Unlike later headings, the presenting verb is explicit here.
Nethanel's 130-weight dish and 70-shekel bowl both contain fine flour with oil. The full repeated gift is preserved.
Nethanel's single incense vessel weighs ten gold units and is filled with incense.
Nethanel's calf, ram and year-old male lamb are each one, for the whole burnt offering.
Nethanel's one male goat is specifically for sin, separate from his deliverance goats.
Nethanel's two heifers and three sets of five match the selected text; ewe lambs remain female and year-old. The closing attribution repeats his father.
Day three identifies Eliab son of Helon as ruler of Zebulun. The verbless heading is retained naturally with a colon.
Eliab's silver vessels carry the same 130 and 70 figures and both flour-and-oil contents; no shortened cross-reference replaces them.
Eliab's gold incense vessel is one, of ten gold units, full of incense.
Eliab's three whole burnt animals are individually one, with year-old applying to the lamb.
Eliab's sin goat remains a separate singular animal.
Eliab's deliverance list preserves two heifers, five rams, five male goats and five year-old ewe lambs, followed by his attribution.
Day four identifies Elizur, Shedeur and Reuben. The presentation order follows the camps, not the initial leader list.
Elizur's dish and bowl retain 130 and 70 sanctuary shekels and both flour-and-oil contents.
Elizur's one incense vessel retains ten gold units and the incense filling.
Elizur's calf, ram and year-old male lamb are each one for whole burning.
Elizur's male goat from the goats is one for sin.
Elizur's two heifers and five each of rams, male goats and year-old ewe lambs are retained with the full attribution.
Day five identifies Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai for Simeon, consistent with the provisional name register.
Shelumiel's two silver vessels retain their respective 130 and 70 weights and identical flour-and-oil filling.
Shelumiel's incense vessel is singular, ten gold units, and filled with incense.
Shelumiel's whole burnt list retains one calf, one ram and one year-old male lamb.
Shelumiel's singular sin goat is not merged with his five deliverance goats.
Shelumiel's deliverance list preserves female heifers and ewe lambs, all four quantities, and the repeated donor attribution.
Day six names Eliasaph son of Reuel for Gad. Reuel follows the selected Greek and is not replaced with Deuel.
Eliasaph's 130-weight dish and 70-shekel bowl retain both flour-and-oil contents and their sacrificial purpose.
Eliasaph's incense vessel is one, of ten gold units, filled with incense.
Eliasaph's calf, ram and year-old male lamb are each one for the whole burnt offering.
Eliasaph's single male goat is for sin.
Eliasaph's two heifers and three groups of five retain sex and age distinctions. The closing attribution again names Reuel.
Day seven identifies Elishama son of Ammihud for Ephraim.
Elishama's silver dish and bowl retain 130 and 70 weights, sanctuary measure and both flour-and-oil fillings.
Elishama's one incense vessel retains ten gold units and full incense contents.
Elishama's whole burnt animals are one calf, one ram and one year-old male lamb.
Elishama's one male goat is specifically the sin offering.
Elishama's deliverance animals preserve two heifers, five rams, five male goats and five year-old ewe lambs, with the donor's father repeated.
Day eight names Gamaliel son of Pedahzur as Manasseh's ruler.
Gamaliel's dish and bowl retain the selected 130 and 70 weights and both oil-prepared flour contents.
Gamaliel's one vessel of ten gold units remains full of incense.
Gamaliel's calf, ram and year-old male lamb are individually one, for whole burning.
Gamaliel's male goat from the goats is one for sin.
Gamaliel's deliverance animals retain all four quantities and the female heifers and ewe lambs. The attribution matches the heading.
Day nine names Abidan son of Gideoni for Benjamin.
Abidan's silver vessels retain 130 and 70 weights and both flour-and-oil contents, without abbreviating the repetitive source.
Abidan's one incense vessel retains ten gold units and the incense filling.
Abidan's one calf, one ram and one year-old male lamb are for the whole burnt offering.
Abidan's one male goat is the sin offering.
Abidan's deliverance list preserves two heifers and five each of the other three animals, including year-old ewe lambs; his father is repeated.
Day ten names Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai as Dan's ruler.
Ahiezer's dish and bowl retain 130 and 70 weights and both fine-flour-and-oil contents.
Ahiezer's one incense vessel is ten gold units, full of incense.
Ahiezer's calf, ram and year-old male lamb each number one for whole burning.
Ahiezer's sin animal is one male goat, distinct from the following goats.
Ahiezer's deliverance list retains two heifers, five rams, five male goats and five year-old ewe lambs, with the closing attribution.
Day eleven identifies Pagiel son of Ocran for Asher.
Pagiel's 130-weight dish and 70-shekel bowl both contain fine flour with oil, as stated individually in this repetition.
Pagiel's single vessel of ten gold units is full of incense.
Pagiel's whole burnt offering includes one calf, one ram and one year-old male lamb.
Pagiel's one male goat is for sin.
Pagiel's deliverance gift preserves the two heifers and all three groups of five, with sex, age and donor attribution intact.
Day twelve names Ahira son of Enan for Naphtali, completing the twelve-day sequence.
Ahira's silver dish and bowl retain 130 and 70 weights and both flour-and-oil contents.
Ahira's incense vessel is one of ten gold units, filled with incense.
Ahira's whole burnt offering retains one calf, one ram and one year-old male lamb.
Ahira's sin offering is one male goat from the goats.
Ahira's deliverance animals preserve two heifers and five each of rams, male goats and year-old ewe lambs. The final donor attribution remains.
The summary counts twelve dishes, twelve bowls and twelve gold incense vessels, matching the twelve presentations.
Each dish is 130 and each bowl 70, giving 2,400 sanctuary shekels for twelve sets. The arithmetic agrees with the stated total.
Twelve incense vessels total 120 gold units, matching twelve times ten. No additional individual-vessel clause from another source is inserted.
Twelve each of calves, rams, year-old male lambs and sin goats are retained. The selected summary includes both sacrifices and drink offerings.
Deliverance totals are twenty-four heifers and sixty each of rams, male goats and year-old ewe lambs; unblemished is explicit here. The unusual filling-of-hands and anointing wording remains.

column2: Moses hears the Lord's voice above the propitiatory cover between two cherubim. The last speaking clause is retained.
